speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Sit, Master Shakespeare. The soft side is toward you, and the jaw may have that and nothing harder.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is quiet today, Mistress. The first Sunday it has been quiet since August. I will not try it further.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The loaf is a penny, and it is a full thumb short of the notch. I set it by the board so you could see the want of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I see it. A penny still, and less bread than the notch was cut for.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence is your board, as it has been, and the firing is the sixpence with the washing. The hall candle is that sixpence. What you burn upstairs is your own.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know my own candles, Mistress. I am not in a humour to burn three.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: The light upstairs is a small thing. A silk thread shows a bad join by a worse light, and a good one by any.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Master Verbeke mends what he is given and does not ask the house where the silk was bought. Eat, the both of you.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is pottage, and the mutton is boiled soft. I kept the crusts off his side of the trencher.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thank you, Alse. Soft is enough.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You were at your book in the church and you did not mark it. I looked. A man who will not mark an almanac is a man saving his hand for the evening.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have a bundle to fair, Mistress, and I shall want a length of red out of your basket when the light is candles. Not the skein. A length.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You may have a length. You may not have the work of my basket, and you may not trail it through the cat.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib is on the settle, not on the Holinshed. I put the book up.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him the settle. He will find the book when he is minded, and the book has survived him before.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: A cat chooses a warm page. I do not argue with a cat.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Mark me, Master Shakespeare. The latch is as it was. I will not have it mended this week because a man is in a hurry for his papers.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not in a hurry for the latch. I am in a hurry for an hour of quiet after dinner, and then for the red.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I can cut the red when you ask. I have cut thread on my arm all summer, and the arm knows the length better than a guess.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: This evening, then. Not now. Let me eat the soft side while it is a kindness and not a lesson.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: It is both. Eat. And if you write to your wife tonight, write before you begin spoiling the page you have just made fair. A letter that waits on a correction waits till Thursday is gone.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thursday's carrier is Thursday. The three lines will be written before I touch the margin again. That is the order.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. Alse, the beer is the small beer. He is not celebrating a tooth.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The small beer is poured.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: I will take the yard after, and leave the table to the paper. A house with two trades in it should keep its hours apart.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Yours and mine, Master Verbeke. I am obliged.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Obliged is a word. The threepence is the fact. Eat your dinner.
